    Engine · the twelve steps

    Statistical Signals

    The owner's twelve-equation framework — demean, normalise, demean across the group, take a short-window expected return in volatility units, strip out what the window's common patterns explain, weight the residual by inverse volatility, scale to gross unity, combine — computed over a named universe — since round 46 the whole market by default, every S&P 500 constituent plus five index rows — on one 60-session window of adjusted closes, with the three choices the equations leave open stated rather than hidden. A rank-weighted residual-momentum read; research output, no execution path.

    What statistical signals are#

    The owner handed the desk a page of twelve equations and one instruction: compute all of this for all of the stocks, and be able to generate it for any stock. The framework is a residual-momentum construction of a classic shape. Take each name's recent daily returns; take out its own mean and its own volatility; take out what the whole group did on each day; measure a short-window expected return in units of the name's volatility; strip out the part of that which the group's common patterns explain; and what is left — the residual — is the signal. Weight the residuals inversely to volatility, scale them so the absolute weights sum to one, and the weighted sum is the combined signal.

    The module is bablytics/collectors/statsignals.py, round 45; round 46 widened its default group from the morning's candidates to the whole market. It implements the equations literally where they are fully specified, and where they are not it makes one definite choice and prints it in the result. This page is the record of both — the equations as the owner wrote them, the desk's reading of each, the three places a choice had to be made, the one consequence the framework carries that is worth naming before anyone reads a weights table, and what that consequence looked like at the top of a five-hundred-name book the first time one was read.

    Research output, no execution path. A statistical signal is a number computed from a window of past returns. It grades nothing, recommends nothing and sizes nothing; the weights sum to one because equation (11) says so, not because anything is being allocated. Nothing in the module, the routes, the panel or the packet places, stages or routes an order of any kind.

    The twelve equations#

    As the owner wrote them, with the framework's own numbering. R(i,s) is name i's simple return on session s, s = 1…M oldest to newest; N is the number of names in the universe. In the result JSON the Greek letters are spelled out — sigma, lambda, epsilon, eta.

    (1)  X(i,s) = R(i,s) − (1/M) · Σ_{s=1..M} R(i,s)          demean each signal's return series
(2)  σ_i² = (1/M) · Σ_{s=1..M} X(i,s)²                     variance of the demeaned returns
(3)  Y(i,s) = X(i,s) / σ_i                                 normalisation
(4)  Y(i,s),  s = 1..M−1                                   truncation to M−1 periods
(5)  Λ(i,s) = Y(i,s) − (1/N) · Σ_{j=1..N} Y(j,s)           cross-sectional demeaning
(6)  Λ(i,s),  s = 1..M−1                                   trimming to the available signal length
(7)  E(i) = (1/d) · Σ_{s=M−d+1..M} R(i,s)                  expected return over an estimation period d
(8)  E_norm(i) = E(i) / σ_i                                volatility-normalised expected return
(9)  E_norm(i) = β · Λ(i,·) + ε(i)                         residual by orthogonalising against the factors Λ
(10) w(i) = η · ε(i) / σ_i                                 weight — the residual, inversely proportioned to volatility
(11) Σ_i |w(i)| = 1                                        weights sum to absolute unity
(12) Combined Signal = Σ_i w(i) · S_i                      the combined signal

    The desk's reading, step by step#

    (1) Demean
    Each name's M returns, less their own average over the window — the last M sessions, sixty by default. What is left is the name's day-to-day movement with its drift taken out.
    (2) Variance
    The mean of the squared demeaned returns. That is the population variance, dividing by M rather than M−1, because that is what the equation says. Its square root σ is the name's daily volatility over the window; the row prints it as sigma_daily_pct.
    (3) Normalise
    Divide the demeaned return by σ. Every name is now in the same units — standard deviations of itself — so a 2% day in a utility and a 2% day in a semiconductor no longer look alike.
    (4) Truncate
    Keep M−1 periods. The framework does not say why, and it does the same again at (6); the module reads the two as one window — the first of the three choices.
    (5) Demean across the group
    On each session, subtract the universe's average z-score from every name's. This is the step that needs a universe: Λ(i,s) is how name i moved relative to the group that day, and it has no meaning for a name on its own.
    (6) Trim
    Again M−1 periods. Same reading as (4).
    (7) Expected return
    The mean of the last d raw returns, ten by default — the framework's word for short-window momentum. Raw returns, not demeaned ones: the equation sums R, not X, and the module does what it says.
    (8) Normalise it
    E divided by σ: momentum in units of the name's own volatility, so a quiet name's 1% and a violent name's 1% are read differently.
    (9) Orthogonalise
    Regress E_norm on the factors Λ and keep the residual ε. The intent is plain — take out of a name's momentum whatever its co-movement with the group explains — but the regression as written cannot be run, which is the second choice.
    (10) Weight
    The residual divided by σ once more, times a scalar η. A name gets weight in proportion to how much unexplained momentum it has, and against how volatile it is.
    (11) Gross unity
    η is whatever makes the absolute weights sum to exactly one. Positive residuals become longs, negative ones shorts; the book is scaled, not sized.
    (12) Combine
    The weighted sum of a per-name signal Si. The framework never says what Si is — the third choice.

    The three choices the framework leaves open#

    Three places the twelve equations are not fully specified. In each the module does one definite thing, says so in its docstring, and reports it in the result so the choice travels with the number.

    (4) and (6): one window, not two truncations#

    The framework truncates to M−1 periods twice, without saying why. The docstring's reading: "M prices give M−1 returns, so the two truncations are read as the SAME window: the module works on the last M daily returns and calls that the window. Nothing is dropped twice." In practice M counts returns, the window is the last M sessions every name in the universe has in common, and (4) and (6) are satisfied by construction rather than by throwing a session away at each step.

    (9): the literal regression is underdetermined#

    Equation (9) regresses N scalars — one E_norm per name — on N rows of Λ, each M long. With M at or above N (sixty sessions, forty names) that is more regressors than observations: in the docstring's words, "underdetermined — a perfect fit and eps ≡ 0 — so it cannot be run as written." A residual that is identically zero is not a signal; it is the regression admitting it had nothing to say.

    Since round 46 the default group is the market — N of 508 against M of 60 — and the literal fit is no longer perfect. It is still not run as written. Sixty regressors on five hundred points would explain about M/(N−1), some 12%, of the momentum by chance alone, and the module reads (9) one way in every universe: the K-component reading below is the same computation whether the group is the day's forty or the whole market, so a read over the sheet and a read over the market differ only in who is in the group, never in the maths.

    What the module does instead: "extracts the K leading principal components of the N×M matrix Lambda (the common return patterns in the window), takes each name's loading on them, and regresses E_norm on those loadings. eps is then the part of a name's volatility-normalised momentum that its exposure to the window's common patterns does not explain — residual momentum." Concretely, a singular value decomposition of Λ; the first K left-singular vectors scaled by their singular values as an N×K matrix of loadings; an intercept column; and an ordinary least-squares fit of E_norm on that. K defaults to 3 and is capped at N−3, so the fit always keeps at least three degrees of freedom. The result's factors block prints K as requested and as used, the fit's R², each component's share of Λ's variance and the fitted betas — "so the reader can see how much the factors took." A universe too small to extract even one component, three names or fewer, gets ε = E_norm minus its cross-sectional mean, and the block says so in words rather than printing a fit that never happened.

    (12): Si is never defined#

    The combined signal is a weighted sum of Si, and Si appears nowhere else in the framework. The docstring: "The module takes S_i := E_norm(i), the quantity the weights were derived from, so the combined signal is the book's weighted volatility-normalised expected return. The alternative S_i := Lambda(i, latest) is available as a parameter." Every result names which it used, as combined_signal_definition, so the number never travels without its definition. Only the default is cached.

    Sigma is divided out twice#

    Named rather than hidden, as the docstring puts it: "(8) divides by sigma once and (10) divides by it again, so a weight scales like E / sigma². The framework overweights low-volatility names quadratically. That is what it says, and that is what is computed."

    It matters when you read a weights table. Two names with the same raw ten-session return and the same unexplained share of it do not get the same weight — the one with half the daily volatility gets roughly four times as much. That is a property of the framework, not a bug in the implementation, and the module does not soften it. If the owner ever wants a single division, that is a change to the equations; it would be made there and recorded here.

    What a very low sigma means#

    The first market read put the tilt on show. The largest weight in the 508-name book — rank 1, w = 0.0134, nearly half again the next name's — went to AES, with a daily σ of 0.20% against a group median of 2.0%. Its ten-session expected return was 0.03% a day, against 0.62% and 0.30% for the two names ranked beneath it: nothing, in raw terms. It is a pinned name — a pending acquisition, its price anchored to the deal terms and moving only as the deal spread does — so the returns in its window are tiny, and dividing a tiny E by a tiny σ, then a tiny residual by that σ again, produces the largest E/σ² in the market. That is the double division at its extreme: the framework does not read AES as the stock with the most unexplained momentum, it reads it as the stock that moves least, and rewards it quadratically for that.

    The threshold is written down in two places that agree: the desk tags a row pinned? and the seats are told to treat its weight as an artefact rather than a signal when σ is under 0.35% a day (board._PINNED_SIGMA_PCT, STATSIG_PINNED_SIGMA in the desk). Nothing in the maths changes; the flag exists so the framework's strongest bias is visible at the moment it fires.

    The maths is not being changed for it. A floor on σ, a rule that drops pinned names, a single division instead of two — each is a change to the equations, and those are the owner's to make; the module computes what the framework says. What the record does instead is make such rows visible: sigma_daily_pct prints on every row beside the weight, and a reader — or a seat — who sees a name at the top of the book with a σ a tenth of the group's should read the weight as the framework's arithmetic about a name that does not move, not as a call on it. Flagged, not removed. The same applies to any name a tender offer, a take-private or a halted tape has pinned inside the window; the AES row is the example the live read happened to hand over.

    The line that says what the factors would have explained by luck#

    Beside r_squared the factors block prints r_squared_expected_if_factors_were_noise, which is K/(N−1). Fitting an intercept and K regressors to N points explains about K/(N−1) of the variance even when the regressors are pure noise — with three components and forty names, roughly 7.7%; with three and the market's 508, 0.6%, which is the 0.006 the live read prints beside its 0.248. So an R² of 0.09 on that universe means the common patterns took almost nothing out of the momentum and the residuals are close to the raw E_norm; an R² of 0.40 means they took a great deal, and the residuals are a genuinely different read. The comparison line exists so nobody reads a small R² as a finding. It is the same instinct as the honest standard error on the special-issue packet: state what the number would be under the null before anyone is impressed by it.

    A read is always inside a universe#

    Steps (5) and (9)–(12) are cross-sectional: they subtract the group's average, extract the group's common patterns, and scale the weights across the group. None of them means anything for one name. So there is no such thing as the statistical signal of NVDA — there is NVDA's row inside a named universe, and the same name gets a different row inside a different universe, because the group mean and the group factors have changed.

    The module enforces this. for_ticker(ticker, universe) adds the name to the universe if it is not already there, runs the whole framework, and returns that name's row together with the universe it was computed in, its size, the factors block and the combined signal. for_universe requires at least two names and refuses with a reason otherwise. Every result names its universe; a row that arrives without one did not come from this module.

    The routes offer four house universes for a per-ticker read, and since round 46 the first is the default: market, every S&P 500 constituent plus five index rows — SPY, QQQ and DIA, the three index ETFs, and ^DJI and ^VIX, the Dow and the VIX themselves; book, the underlying tickers of the latest completed run's leads; core, the options scanner's core names; and both, the union of book and core, which was the default through round 45. The reply carries a universe_selection block — which one, how many from each, and the run it read the book from — so the provenance of the group is on the record beside the group itself.

    The market universe, and where its names come from#

    The owner's round-46 ask was to expand the read "so it includes all five hundred stocks in the S&P 500 as well as indices, like the QQQ, SPY, and DJA and the VIX". market_universe() in the module is that list: the five index rows first, in the order INDEX_ROWS declares them, then every name in config.UNIVERSE — 503 constituents, not 500, because the index carries dual share classes — for 508 names. for_market(**kw) is for_universe over it. The constituent list is a dated snapshot, not a live membership: bablytics/universe.py bakes one taken from Wikipedia's "List of S&P 500 companies" on 2026-08-18, and python -m bablytics.universe refresh re-fetches the page and writes data/universe.json, which takes precedence when present (the refresh of 2026-09-13 also gave 503). A name that joined the index after the snapshot is not in the group until the next refresh, and a name that left it stays until then; the group is what the list said on its date, and every result names its members so the reader can see which list it was.

    The "DJA" in the ask is read twice, on purpose. DIA is the ETF that tracks the Dow and can be traded; ^DJI is the average itself and cannot. The framework wants the index's own returns in the group and the desk wants a row a lead could actually be expressed in, so both are rows, and the same goes for the VIX: ^VIX is the index — there is no share of it — and the row is there so the market's fear gauge is read beside the names, not so anyone buys it.

    Every row now says what it is. kind_of(ticker) returns stock, etf or index; the row carries it as kind; the result counts the group as universe_kinds — on the live read {"stock": 503, "etf": 3, "index": 2} — and pulls the five index rows out into an indices block so a reader sees the market's own residual momentum without scanning five hundred names for it. for_ticker's reply carries both. The tag exists so that nothing — no seat, no panel, no later round — reads a weight on ^VIX or ^DJI as a position; the ETFs are the tradeable proxies, and their rows say etf for the same reason. The cache schema was bumped with the change, so a per-day file the round-45 build wrote is ignored rather than served back without the tags.

    Why five index rows cannot distort a group of five hundred#

    The natural worry is that ^VIX — which moves 6–7% on an ordinary day against a stock's 1–2% — would dominate every cross-sectional step it touches. It cannot, and the reason is in the order of the equations. Steps (1)–(3) put every name into units of its own volatility before anything cross-sectional happens: a 6.6% VIX day and a 1.5% bank day are both a one-sigma move, and it is one-sigma moves, Y(i,s), that step (5) averages across the group and that step (9) extracts common patterns from. The VIX's row sits on the same scale as every stock's inside (5) and (9) — one row of 508 in the group mean and one row of 508 in the factor extraction — and its z-scores run against the group's more often than with them, which is simply a pattern for the factors to find, not a distortion of them. Then (10) divides by σ once more, so a name with a daily σ of 6.6% gets, for the same residual, a weight five and a half times smaller than a name at 1.2%, and for the same raw ten-session return some thirty times smaller. On the live read ^VIX's weight was 0.00006 in absolute terms, ranked 262 of 508 — a row that is present, read, and harmless.

    The market read, measured#

    Measured on 2026-09-13 over the whole universe, window ending on the 2026-09-11 close: 508 names, 0 excluded — every constituent and every index row had sixty common sessions. The first read of the day took 16 seconds, all of it the coupling cache's eight-thread prefetch of some five hundred series it had not yet fetched; the second read, served from the per-day file, took under a tenth of a second. K = 3 was used as requested, and the three components explained R² 0.248 of the volatility-normalised momentum against 0.006 if they had been noise — forty times the null, which is the market's common patterns being real. SPY ranked 176 of 508 with a weight of 0.0008; QQQ 299, DIA 242, ^DJI 286, ^VIX 262 — the market's own rows in the middle of the book, which is where a residual read should put the thing every residual was taken against. The largest weight went to AES, and the section on a very low sigma is about why.

    The data#

    Daily simple returns on adjusted closes, shared with the coupling collector's cache — one year of daily history per name, the same prefetch, the same per-day file. The sharing is deliberate: two collectors fetching the same year of the same tickers separately would double the feed calls and could disagree on a return.

    Adjusted rather than raw is a choice with a reason, and it is the opposite of the choice the court makes. The docstring: "For a rolling statistical window adjusted closes are the right series — a dividend is not a return event and a split must not print as a −50% day — unlike the court's scoring path, which compares against a raw morning quote and therefore uses raw closes." The Evening Court and the outcomes recorder (training/outcomes.py, fetched with auto_adjust=False) measure a lead from the price the board actually saw at 7:00 to the price on the tape later; adjusting either side would score a dividend as a loss against a quote that never included it. A sixty-session covariance window has the opposite need. Both are right for what they do, and the two series are not mixed.

    The window is the last M sessions of the union of every name's dates. A name missing any of them — too short a history, a listing gap — is left out and appears in excluded with the reason, as does a name with no variance in the window. Exclusion is reported, never silent, because the group mean in (5) changes with who is in the group.

    The parameters, and what changing them does#

    ParameterDefaultRoute acceptsWhat it is, and what moving it does
    M6010 – 250Sessions in the window. Longer: σ and the factors are estimated over more data and move more slowly, so the read is smoother and older. Shorter: more responsive, noisier, and the factor extraction has fewer sessions to find a pattern in. A universe needs M common sessions; a name with fewer is excluded. The module's own floor is 5.
    d101 – MSessions in the expected-return window of (7) — the momentum horizon. Very short and the "expected return" is a few sessions' move, which is as often noise as trend; longer and it is slower momentum. The module clamps it to the window.
    K30 – 10 (K=0 takes no factor out and says so; epsilon is then E_norm minus its cross-sectional mean)Principal components in (9). More components explain more of E_norm and leave smaller residuals — at the limit every residual is zero and the framework says nothing. Fewer leave more of the group's co-movement inside the signal. Capped at N−3; the result prints K_requested and K_used separately, and 0 gives the small-universe fallback.
    s_ie_norme_norm · lambda_latestWhat (12) sums. The alternative is not cached.

    The route refuses a parameter outside its range with a 400 rather than clamping it. The module clamps quietly — d into the window, K to N−3, an unknown s_i to the default — which is right for a library and would hide a typo from a caller of the API.

    The parameters are part of the cache key, and so is the schema version. A result computed with M=60, d=10, K=3 for one universe on one day is written to data/cache/statsignals-<date>-<hash>.json and served back until the date changes; a different universe, a different parameter or a different as_of is a different file, and a file written under an older schema — round 46 bumped it when the rows gained their kind — is ignored rather than served. Every result says whether it was computed or came from cache.

    What a row holds#

    FieldEquationMeaning
    kind—stock, etf or index: what the row is, since round 46. A weight on an index row is not a position anyone could hold
    sigma_daily_pct(2)σi, the name's daily volatility over the window, in percent
    x_latest_pct(1)X(i, M): the most recent demeaned return, in percent
    y_latest(3)Y(i, M): the most recent z-score against the name's own window
    lambda_latest(5)Λ(i, M): the most recent z-score less the group's that day
    e_pct(7)E(i): the mean of the last d raw returns, in percent
    e_norm(8)E_norm(i): that, in units of σi
    epsilon(9)ε(i): the residual momentum once the window's common patterns are taken out
    weight(10) (11)w(i), signed; the absolute weights sum to one across the universe
    rank—1 is the largest positive weight, N the most negative
    side—long, short or flat, by the sign of the weight

    Around the rows, the universe-level fields: parameters, universe and n; since round 46 universe_kinds, the count of the group by kind, and indices, the five index rows pulled out where a reader can find them; the factors block; eta and gross_weight (1.0 unless every residual is zero, in which case the weights are zero and a note says so); combined_signal with its combined_signal_definition; excluded with a reason per name; notes; and as_of, data and source, which say which session the window ends on, what series was used, and whether the file came from the cache.

    Where the numbers appear#

    The morning packet, and every seat's prompt
    As of round 45 the framework is run once per morning and the whole row rides on each candidate, persisting with the lead as features.stat_signals, so a lead can be read back later with the numbers it was graded beside. Through round 45 the group was that morning's candidates — the sheet being graded, so every number was relative to the other names on it. Since round 46 the group is the market: the framework is run once over every S&P 500 constituent plus the five index rows, each candidate's row is looked up in that result, so its rank is its place among five hundred rather than among twenty, and the shared block carries the index rows — each tagged by kind — so every seat sees the market's own residual momentum beside the candidates' and none reads a weight on ^VIX as a position. A candidate outside the S&P 500 and the index rows is not added to the group the way the per-ticker route adds one; it gets no row and a clause saying it was not in the market universe, which is a fact about the group and not a fetch failure, and the clause says which. In the prompts the two halves travel separately: every seat — graders, Skeptic, Executive — gets one shared summary block (the window, the factors taken out and how much they explained beside what noise alone would have, the combined signal with its definition, the index rows), and each name's JSON row carries one bracketed clause — σ per day, E_norm, ε, the signed weight and rank out of N. A name the framework excluded says why instead of printing blanks, and a morning the collector failed prints an explicit not-ok block rather than silence, because a seat told nothing infers something. It is a number for the seats to weigh beside the tape, the flow and the headlines; it is not a grade and not a stance, and the house rule on the briefing page says so.
    The Research Desk
    A panel on the Research Desk shows the named ticker's row inside a house universe — the market by default since round 46 — with the universe named and counted by kind, so the read can be generated for any stock the way the owner asked.
    GET /api/signals/statistical?tickers=…
    The whole result for a universe you name — two to eighty comma-separated tickers — with M, d, K and s_i as optional query parameters. Every row, the factors block, the combined signal, the exclusions and the notes. A 404 carries the module's reason and every exclusion when the data leaves fewer than two usable names.
    GET /api/signals/statistical/<ticker>?universe=market|book|core|both
    One name's row, computed inside the chosen house universe — the market since round 46 unless another is named — with the ticker added if absent, and the universe, its size and its count by kind, the factors block, the combined signal, the five index rows and the universe_selection block returned alongside. A name the data excluded is a 404 with the reason, not an empty row.

    Both routes are authenticated like every other router (Depends(require_auth)) and both are reads: market data through the shared cache, the collector's own per-day file under data/cache/, no database writes. Neither imports anything under the broker package.

    What a combined signal is not#

    It is not a forecast. E(i) is a ten-session average of what already happened; nothing in the twelve steps looks forward, and the framework's own name for the quantity — expected return — should be read as the statistician's word, not as a prediction. It is not advice, and it is not a position: the weights sum to one because equation (11) says so, not because anything is sized to anyone's account. And it is not the board's view — no seat wrote it, the Executive does not sign it, the Skeptic does not cross-examine it. It is a rank-weighted residual-momentum read over one sixty-session window: which names in this group have moved, in units of their own volatility, more than their co-movement with the group explains, and by how much. Read it as that, beside the grades rather than instead of them. And a weight on ^VIX or ^DJI is not a position that could exist: those rows are in the default group so the market's own residual momentum is visible beside the names, each is tagged index so nothing reads it as one, and the ETFs beside them are the proxies a lead would actually be written in.

    Research output, no execution path. The module, the two routes and the panel compute and display. Nothing they produce is an order, a stage or a size, and nothing they touch can reach a venue.
